articles.title: Mary Fowler ruled out of Matildas friendlies due to ‘personal circumstances’
articles.summary: Manchester City attacker to miss Germany and Haiti games. Charlton midfielder Leah Davidson called into Australia squad. Matildas star Mary Fowler has been ruled out of upcoming friendly matches against Germany and Haiti due to personal circumstances.
body: Football Australia confirmed on Tuesday morning Fowler would not feature in the upcoming international window, with four-cap Charlton midfielder Leah Davidson called up in her place.

“Mary Fowler has been withdrawn from the October international window due to personal circumstances,” FA said in a statement. “The decision was made following discussions between Fowler, Manchester City and Matildas staff.”
Fowler’s absence is a blow for coach Joe Montemurro ahead of the two important friendlies.
The 23-year-old has been in terrific form for club Manchester City and likely would have played a key role in both games as Australia’s best creative attacking player.
points: Matildas star Mary Fowler has been ruled out of upcoming friendly matches against Germany and Haiti due to personal circumstances.
Football Australia confirmed on Tuesday morning Fowler would not feature in the upcoming international window, with four-cap Charlton midfielder Leah Davidson called up in her place.

articles.title: Nations League roundup: Olise leads late charge as France bowl over Belgium
articles.summary: France score four goals in 14 minutes to triumph. Italy see off Turkey, Hungary edge out Ukraine. Michael Olise came off the bench to inspire France to a 4-1 win over Belgium in the Nations League, handing Zinedine Zidane his first home victory since taking charge.
body: Dodi Lukébakio put Belgium on course for their first competitive win over Les Bleus in 45 years when he fired the visitors in front in the first half at the Stade de France. But the hosts turned the match on its head in a blistering finish, scoring four times in 14 minutes to preserve Zidane’s unbeaten start and move closer to the quarter-finals.

Désiré Doué hauled France level in the 77th minute with a low drive from the edge of the area before Olise teed up Rayan Cherki to fire them ahead four minutes later. Olise then put the result beyond doubt with a third goal before adding another in stoppage time to cap a stunning French comeback.

France, who also beat Belgium 1-0 in Brussels last week thanks to a late goal from Olise, moved three points clear of Italy at the top of Group A1, with Belgium another point back. Italy beat Turkey 3-1 in Bologna to condemn their opponents to a fourth straight loss, goals from Gianluca Scamacca, Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito doing the business.

articles.title: How did some City fans become aggressive defenders of a nation state’s regime? | Sean Ingle
articles.summary: The Manchester City case is one example of how fandom has warped beyond previous boundaries in online spaces. A video of Liam Gallagher playing in a 1996 charity football match resurfaced on social media recently.
body: As the fallout from the biggest scandal in British football history headed into a second week, Gallagher was asked what he made of rival fans wanting City to lose all their trophies after being found guilty of all the serious charges against them. “There all NEUROTIC little GIMPS,” came the reply on social media. It was one of dozens of sweary, punchy, and often amusing responses, all built on a solitary article of faith: that City will somehow find a way to wriggle free.

But Gallagher is hardly standing alone. Over at Bluemoon, the biggest City forum, the tone has been just as defiant – albeit with a sprinkle of gallows humour. “Have we been blamed for the Titanic hitting the iceberg yet?” asked one user. “Manchester City shot JFK,” wrote another. “This isn’t just a fight between the PL & City. It’s a fight for the heart, soul & future of football,” reckoned a third.

Staggeringly, the forum now has over 192,000 posts since the initial charges against City, dating back to 2023. Naturally the Premier League, jealous rivals and the media all come under heavy fire. Yet there remains a curious reluctance among fans to accept wrongdoing – or to criticise the club’s owners.

articles.title: Humble Gilmour happy with new role as 50th cap beckons
articles.summary: Billy Gilmour is excited by the prospect of earning a 50th Scotland cap after a key role in Sebastien Pocognoli's first win as national head coach.
body: Still fresh-faced, still slight of stature, still to reach the peak of his powers after a career blighted by untimely injuries, it is hard to believe Billy Gilmour is already on the brink of a 50th cap for Scotland.
The 25-year-old midfielder at last is winning the regular first-team starts, not only with the national team but also with Napoli, his talent surely deserves.
His cause has, ironically, been aided in part by the absence through illness from both of clubmate Scott McTominay.
It has also certainly encouraged new national head coach Sebastien Pocognoli to urge Gilmour to take the kind of more advanced positions his fellow midfielder occupied under predecessor Steve Clarke.

articles.title: NFL suspends official involved in Cardinals McBride’s tirade
articles.summary: The NFL didn’t take long to make a decision on two officials from this past weekend. They suspended line judge Jeff Seeman, who was involved in an incident involving Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride, and also referee Adrian Hill who had yelled at Minnesota Vikings LB Eric Wilson.
body: Regarding the McBride incident, there was a third-and-two pass attempt from QB Jacoby Brissett and McBride as time was winding down in the fourth quarter against the New York Football Giants.

Brissett dropped back to pass, and flung it in the direction of McBride just past the first down marker on the left side. Giants nickelback Dru Phillips picked up McBride off the line, grabbed his jersey, released, and was able to bat away the pass. He was obviously all over McBride and made physical contact without the tight end catching the ball.
Before the ball even arrived, McBride was falling to the turf. For one, McBride is not a guy who flops. For another, he doesn’t fall without something making him.

Seeman was in a good position to see the play as he was standing at the 13-yard line. No flag from Seeman or the back judge, who was stationed behind Brissett and the offense. McBride then got up and walked towards Seeman, and the two jawed at each other. It is uncertain what was said, but a sideline camera captured Seeman yelling at McBride, “F*** you!” twice, if you can read lips. McBride then pointed to the camera and was pulled away from the situation by Cardinals personnel.

articles.title: Eagles injury list grows: Cam Jurgens enters concussion protocol
articles.summary: The list of injured Eagles players continues to grow, and things are getting particularly dicey up front with the offensive line. It was reported Monday night that former center turned left guard Cam Jurgens self-reported concussion symptoms earlier in the day, and is now in the protocol, according…
body: Sunday’s game against the Rams really highlighted what a bad position the Eagles are in with their OL depth, and Jurgens being sidelined only adds to the issue. The new left guard stepped into Landon Dickerson’s spot when the original LG went to IR after Week 1, but Jurgens really struggled in his new role. Head coach Nick Sirianni was asked on Monday if they had considered benching Jurgens, but he publicly stated he was pleased with Jurgens.

Heading into training camp, the Eagles offensive line was Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, and Lane Johnson. Heading into their Week 4 game against the Rams, the starting OL was Jordan Mailata, Cam Jurgens, Drew Kendall, Tyler Steen, and Markel Bell.

Lane Johnson missed Sunday’s game due to personal reasons, and Fred Johnson was inactive due to injury. Drew Kendall went into the medical tent at one point during the game, but was thankfully able to return and finish the game, but there’s a chance he’s not fully healthy either.
Heading into the week the team had just Willie Lampkin and Micah Morris as active backups, and they’ll have to turn to one of them to replace Jurgens if he’s unable to travel to London.

Jamie Donley and Josh Magennis also brought saves out of Mamardashvili and Tom Atcheson felt he had should have had a first-half penalty, but Northern Ireland were held to a stalemate for the second time in a week at Windsor Park.

Georgia, still yet to score in this season's Nations League, responded to their 1-0 loss to Northern Ireland in Tbilisi 11 days ago by sacking Willy Sagnol, but Ramaz Svanadze is still awaiting his first win in charge despite Khvicha Kvaratskhelia showing flashes of his brilliance in the second half.

Northern Ireland started the night as the only side yet to concede in this season's Nations League, and Pierce Charles made big saves from Zuriko Davitashvili and Giorgi Tsitaishvili to make it four competitive clean sheets in a row for the first time since 2017.

articles.title: Is Ben Johnson Bears' Most Important Piece? Why Last 2 Games Suggest He Might Be
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are 3-1 and have won three games this season with three different starting quarterbacks. With that, Colin Cowherd believes Sunday's performance is the latest piece of evidence of who matters most in Chicago: Head coach Ben Johnson.
body: "It is a quarterback-first league, but the guy who builds the culture is the coach," Cowherd said on Monday's "The Herd." "I think we've discovered in the last two weeks, as gifted as Caleb Williams is, the centerpiece of the Bears is Ben Johnson."

With quarterback Caleb Williams sidelined for a second straight game with a right hamstring injury, the Bears won against the New York Jets 23-12. Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent, who threw for 268 yards, and second-year running back Kyle Monangai, who carried a career-high 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns, led the way in the victory.

"Yesterday, a backup running back, a seventh-round running back, with a backup quarterback. Once again, it's 400-plus yards. I mean, they had more first downs than the Jets had plays," Cowherd said. "So don't look at the 23-12 score. This could have been 50-12. It was not competitive."

New York finished with just 157 yards and seven first downs and went 0-for-7 on third down. Cowherd pointed to the time of possession, with the Bears holding the ball for nearly 43 minutes, calling it, "like a lopsided college time of possession differential."
points: The Chicago Bears are 3-1 and have won three games this season with three different starting quarterbacks.
With that, Colin Cowherd believes Sunday's performance is the latest piece of evidence of who matters most in Chicago: Head coach Ben Johnson.
"It is a quarterback-first league, but the guy who builds the culture is the coach," Cowherd said on Monday's "The Herd.
"I think we've discovered in the last two weeks, as gifted as Caleb Williams is, the centerpiece of the Bears is Ben Johnson."
